The IRA itself was substantially amended by the OBBBA (described below) on July 4, 2025, including with respect to the Section 48E and the Section 45X Credit, in a manner which materially reduced the future availability of these credits.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release; it is management's expectation, not a result.
growth_thesis.claim: Management's guidance points to continued growth. The FY2027 revenue outlook was raised to $4.2 to $4.45 billion from $4.1 to $4.4 billion, and Q3 revenue is guided to approximately 10% year-over-year growth. For this to hold, backlog conversion and acquired revenue must arrive as planned.
quotes: Updated outlook includes Q3 FY27 revenue at approximately 10% year over year growth, and Q3 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin roughly 1 to 2 percentage points below Q4 FY27.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as management's belief in the 10-K; no data in the evidence quantifies the effect on orders.
growth_thesis.claim: The company ties long-term demand to rising electricity use from data centers and electrification. For this to continue, solar must stay cost-competitive and grid interconnection and permitting must not limit new projects.
quotes: Global electricity demand is entering a period of accelerated growth driven by factors such as data center expansion, increased use of artificial intelligence, and electrification of transportation and buildings.
At the same time, the expansion of electricity supply is constrained by factors including transmission and interconnection limitations, permitting timelines, and availability of grid infrastructure.

material_events.claim: The company acquired Prevalon, a U.S. provider of large-scale battery energy storage and power stabilization solutions, for cash and deferred stock consideration.
quotes: On July 17, 2026, we acquired 100% of the ownership interests in Prevalon, a U.S.-headquartered provider of large-scale BESS, power stabilization solutions, and lifecycle services for a combination of cash and deferred stock consideration.

material_events.claim: The company bought complementary assets of Zigor Corporation's power conversion business and its U.S. subsidiary Apex Power in an all-cash transaction.
quotes: Additionally, on July 30, 2026, as part of an all-cash transaction, we acquired 100% of complementary assets of Zigor Corporation’s power conversion business and its U.S.-based subsidiary, Apex Power.

material_events.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A, and the earnings release also reports the completion.
material_events.claim: The company completed its acquisition of Zimmermann PV-Steel Group for total consideration of up to 230 million Euros in cash.
quotes: On October 21, 2026, we completed the previously announced acquisition of Zimmermann PV-Steel Group (“Zimmermann”), for total consideration of up to 230 million Euros in cash

material_events.basis: Stated in the earnings release table.
material_events.claim: With its Q2 FY27 results, the company published an updated FY2027 outlook with a higher revenue range than before.
quotes: Revenue | $4.2 to $4.45 billion | $4.1 to $4.4 billion

material_events.basis: Stated in the earnings release and shown in the cash flow statement.
material_events.claim: The company repurchased common stock during the six months ended October 2, 2026, and the CFO said about $162 million was returned to shareholders through repurchases. The prior-year period shows no repurchases.
quotes: We ended the quarter with over $1 billion of cash and cash equivalents and no debt, while funding new acquisitions and returning approximately $162 million to shareholders through share repurchases.

material_events.claim: The Board expanded its size and appointed Sarah Slusser and Michael Alvarez as directors.
quotes: On October 26, 2026, the Board of Directors (the “Board”) of the Company increased the size of the Board from ten to twelve and appointed Sarah Slusser and Michael Alvarez to serve as directors of the Company.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factor; the timing and size of the effect on the company are not stated.
risks.claim: Federal law changes shortened the window for the solar tax credits that the company's customers rely on. The 10-K says this will likely reduce overall project volume over time, which would cut demand for trackers.
quotes: Such acceleration in the expiration of these tax credits will reduce the number of projects in future years that would have otherwise qualified for such credits, likely reducing the overall project volume over time.

risks.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the 10-K; the sensitivity of margins to the credits is inferred.
risks.claim: Results depend on IRA 45X credit vendor rebates, which are netted into the cost of sales, and the 10-K says the OBBBA materially reduced the future availability of these credits. The latest quarter included about $99 million of these rebates and tariffs, net.
quotes: Q2 FY27, Q1 FY27, and Q2 FY26 results include approximately $99 million, $99 million, and $67 million, respectively, of IRA 45X advanced manufacturing tax credit vendor rebates and tariffs, net.

The IRA itself was substantially amended by the OBBBA (described below) on July 4, 2025, including with respect to the Section 48E and the Section 45X Credit, in a manner which materially reduced the future availability of these credits.

risks.basis: The margin figures are stated in the release; the pricing and mix mechanism is inferred from the risk factor and the revenue-mix commentary.
risks.claim: Gross margin is under pressure. GAAP gross margin was 31.1% in the latest quarter against 32.4% a year earlier and 35.9% in the prior quarter. The 10-K warns that price competition could hurt margins.
quotes: This may result in price competition, including downward pressure on pricing, which could adversely affect our revenue and margins.

risks.basis: The risk is stated in the 10-Q; the link to the receivable balance is inferred from the balance sheet.
risks.claim: The company depends on a small number of customers, and receivables are growing. A loss, non-performance or payment default by a significant customer would hit revenue and cash flow. Accounts receivable rose to 584,299 from 417,043 (table in thousands).
quotes: A loss of one or more of our significant customers, their inability to perform under their contracts, or their default in payment, could harm our business and negatively impact our revenue, results of operations and cash flows.

risks.basis: The conversion and timing risks are stated in the filings; applying them to the outlook is inferred.
risks.claim: The raised annual outlook depends on converting a backlog above $6 billion into revenue, and delays in large projects can move revenue between quarters. Results for a given period could therefore fall short of expectations.
quotes: Because we recognize revenue on projects as legal title to equipment is transferred from us to the customer, any delays in large projects from one quarter to another may cause our results of operations for a particular period to fall below expectations.
We may not be able to convert our orders in backlog into revenue.

risks.basis: The acquisitions and balances are stated in the filings; the integration risk is the 10-Q risk factor applied to them.
risks.claim: Acquisition activity is accelerating and moves the company into new product areas (energy storage, power conversion, steel). Goodwill rose to 653,594 from 488,950 (table in thousands). A further acquisition, Zimmermann, closed after quarter-end for up to 230 million Euros in cash. This raises integration and cash-use risk.
quotes: Future acquisitions, strategic investments, strategic transactions, partnerships, joint ventures or alliances could be difficult to identify and integrate, divert the attention of key management personnel, disrupt our business, dilute stockholder value and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
